a: There is no reliable rule that this helps, and it can lose a listing's sales history. Improve the existing listing first, unless you have a specific reason to relist.
t: eBay SEO for UK Sellers: How to Get Your Listings Found and Chosen

q: Do free delivery listings rank better?
a: Delivery terms can affect buyer choice and overall appeal, but no single delivery option guarantees a higher position. Compare the total cost and protect your margin.
t: eBay SEO for UK Sellers: How to Get Your Listings Found and Chosen

q: Can an agency manage eBay SEO for me?
a: Yes, an agency can review and improve your listings, although you stay responsible for accurate product information and for meeting eBay's rules. Agree who approves changes and who handles customer service.
t: eBay SEO for UK Sellers: How to Get Your Listings Found and Chosen

q: What is the difference between a CRO audit and a website audit?
a: The term website audit can mean many things, often technical health or SEO. A conversion audit focuses specifically on how visitors behave and what stops them taking a chosen action, though it may flag technical issues that affect this.
t: What a Conversion Rate Optimisation Audit Covers

q: Do I need a lot of traffic for an audit to be useful?
a: Not necessarily. Lower traffic limits how much you can conclude from analytics and A/B tests, but qualitative research, journey reviews and fixing clear problems can still be valuable. The audit should be adapted to the data you have.
t: What a Conversion Rate Optimisation Audit Covers

q: Can I do a conversion audit myself?
a: You can do a useful first pass by checking your tracking, trying your own forms on a phone and reading customer questions. An outside reviewer brings a fresh view, because it is hard to see your own site as a newcomer would.
t: What a Conversion Rate Optimisation Audit Covers

q: How much access will an auditor need?
a: Usually read-only access to analytics and any testing or recording tools, plus an idea of your sales or enquiry data. Share access in line with your own security and data protection policies, and remove it once it is no longer needed.
t: What a Conversion Rate Optimisation Audit Covers

q: Will an audit guarantee more sales?
a: No. An audit identifies likely problems and opportunities, but results depend on what you implement, your offer and your market. Treat any guarantee of a specific uplift with caution.
t: What a Conversion Rate Optimisation Audit Covers

q: Is brand strategy part of marketing strategy?
a: Some people treat it that way, but it is usually more useful to see brand strategy as a wider business foundation. It can affect hiring, customer service and product decisions as well as marketing. Marketing strategy then builds on it.
t: Brand Strategy vs Marketing Strategy: What Is the Difference for a UK Business?

q: Can I have a marketing strategy without a brand strategy?
a: Yes, and many businesses do, at least informally. The risk is inconsistent messaging and a greater reliance on price. Even a brief statement of who you serve and why they should choose you can help.
t: Brand Strategy vs Marketing Strategy: What Is the Difference for a UK Business?

q: Does a small business need a brand strategy?
a: It needs the answers, though not necessarily a formal project. Being clear on your audience, your difference and your tone can be enough to begin with. You can build on this as the business grows.
t: Brand Strategy vs Marketing Strategy: What Is the Difference for a UK Business?

q: Who should own each strategy?
a: In smaller businesses, the owner or leadership team usually needs to be closely involved in brand decisions, since they affect the whole company. Marketing strategy often sits with a marketing lead or an agency, working to goals agreed with leadership.
t: Brand Strategy vs Marketing Strategy: What Is the Difference for a UK Business?

q: How often should each be reviewed?
a: There is no fixed rule. Marketing plans tend to be reviewed regularly, as results and budgets change. Brand strategy usually needs a fresh look when something significant shifts, such as your market, offer or ownership.
t: Brand Strategy vs Marketing Strategy: What Is the Difference for a UK Business?

q: How do I start selling on B&Q Marketplace?
a: Check B&Q's current seller information for eligibility and the application process. Requirements may change and can differ by product type, so rely on the official guidance.
t: B&Q Marketplace SEO: How to Improve Your Product Listings

q: Are marketplace listings the same as Google SEO?
a: They share some principles, such as matching customer language and being accurate. However, a marketplace works with its own product data, filters and seller information, so complete attributes are particularly important.
t: B&Q Marketplace SEO: How to Improve Your Product Listings

q: How long should a product title be?
a: Follow any limit in your current seller guidance. Within that, include what a buyer needs to recognise the product and tell it apart, and avoid repeating keywords.
t: B&Q Marketplace SEO: How to Improve Your Product Listings

q: Can I reuse descriptions from my own website?
a: You can use them as a starting point if your rules allow it. Do check that the details suit the marketplace format, and that the fields and attributes are completed separately.
t: B&Q Marketplace SEO: How to Improve Your Product Listings

q: Do customer reviews matter?
a: Reviews can influence buying decisions. Focus on accurate listings and reliable delivery, respond to feedback sensibly and do not try to obtain fake or incentivised reviews against the rules.
t: B&Q Marketplace SEO: How to Improve Your Product Listings

q: How should I measure improvements?
a: Compare views, conversion, sales and returns for the products you changed, using whatever reports your seller account provides. Change batches of products at a time, so you can see what made a difference.
t: B&Q Marketplace SEO: How to Improve Your Product Listings

q: Is a bespoke website better for SEO than a template?
a: Not by itself. Search performance depends on factors such as content, structure, speed and reputation. A custom build gives you more control, but a well-made template site can perform well, and a poorly built custom site can perform badly.
t: Bespoke Website Design Agency UK: When It Is Worth It and How to Choose

q: Can I edit a bespoke website myself?
a: It should be possible if it is planned from the start. Ask for a content management system that suits your team, and a demonstration of the editing process before you commit.
t: Bespoke Website Design Agency UK: When It Is Worth It and How to Choose

q: Does bespoke mean custom code?
a: Not necessarily. Many custom designs are built on established platforms such as WordPress or Shopify, which can reduce cost and make future changes easier. Ask each provider how its version works.
t: Bespoke Website Design Agency UK: When It Is Worth It and How to Choose

q: Should I get a brand designed first?
a: If your brand is unclear or outdated, it usually helps to sort it first, or as part of the same project. Your positioning and identity shape the design decisions that follow.
t: Bespoke Website Design Agency UK: When It Is Worth It and How to Choose

q: Can a bespoke site grow with my business?
a: Yes, if it is built from reusable components and on a suitable platform. Tell the agency about any plans for new services, products or locations so that they can plan for them.
t: Bespoke Website Design Agency UK: When It Is Worth It and How to Choose

q: What if I already have a template site?
a: You may not need to start again. Improving the content and fixing the weakest pages might be enough. If the template is genuinely holding you back, a redesign can reuse your best content.
t: Bespoke Website Design Agency UK: When It Is Worth It and How to Choose

q: Is AI-written content bad for SEO?
a: Not automatically. The bigger risk is publishing inaccurate, thin or generic pages, however they were produced. Have a knowledgeable person review anything before it goes live, and add the first-hand detail only your business can provide.
t: AI SEO Agency UK: What They Really Do and How to Choose One

q: Will AI SEO get results faster?
a: AI can speed up research and preparation, but rankings still depend on factors such as competition, your site's strength and how search engines respond. Be wary of anyone who promises a fixed timescale for rankings.
t: AI SEO Agency UK: What They Really Do and How to Choose One

q: Is AI SEO the same as GEO?
a: No. AI SEO generally means using AI to carry out search optimisation, while GEO aims to make your brand visible and cited in AI-generated answers. Some providers offer both, so ask which is included.
t: AI SEO Agency UK: What They Really Do and How to Choose One

q: Do I still need ordinary SEO?
a: Yes. Crawlable pages, clear structure, useful content and a trustworthy reputation remain the foundation. AI changes how some of the work gets done rather than removing the need for it.
t: AI SEO Agency UK: What They Really Do and How to Choose One

q: Can my own team do this with AI tools?
a: Often, for some tasks. A capable team can use AI for drafting and research. An agency may add value through technical experience, a wider view of search and the time to keep the work moving.
t: AI SEO Agency UK: What They Really Do and How to Choose One

q: How do I measure whether it is working?
a: Look at the search performance of the pages you care about, then at the enquiries or sales they bring in. Output figures, such as the number of pages produced, show activity rather than results.
t: AI SEO Agency UK: What They Really Do and How to Choose One

q: Is a WordPress export the same as a backup?
a: No. An export covers content and leaves out themes, plugins, settings and more. A backup should cover your files and database, so keep regular backups regardless.
t: WordPress Import and Export Tools: Moving Content Between Sites Safely

q: Does the export file contain my images?
a: Generally not. It records details of media items and their addresses, and the importer can then fetch them from the original site if that site can still be reached.
t: WordPress Import and Export Tools: Moving Content Between Sites Safely

q: Will importing overwrite my existing content?
a: An import normally adds content and does not replace existing items, though matches may be skipped. Always take a backup first, as results depend on your content.
t: WordPress Import and Export Tools: Moving Content Between Sites Safely

q: Can I import content from Wix or another platform?
a: The tools listed under Import may include options for some other systems, but support varies. For one common example, see our guide to moving from Wix to WordPress.
t: WordPress Import and Export Tools: Moving Content Between Sites Safely

q: Can I export just one category?
a: Usually yes. Choose Posts on the export screen and filter by category. Some related items may need separate attention, so check the result on a test site.
t: WordPress Import and Export Tools: Moving Content Between Sites Safely

q: Can I export online shop products this way?
a: Products can appear as a content type, but shop data is more complex, and orders in particular may be stored differently. Treat shop moves as a separate project and test thoroughly.
t: WordPress Import and Export Tools: Moving Content Between Sites Safely

q: Do I have to have a blog page in WordPress?
a: No. You can set a static homepage and leave the Posts page dropdown unselected. Your posts are not deleted by this, so if you already have some, review how they can still be reached.
t: WordPress Front Page and Posts Page: How to Set Your Homepage and Blog

q: Why is my blog page blank in the editor?
a: The posts page is usually left empty because WordPress fills it with your post listing on the live site. A blank editor is normal, and it does not mean your posts have been lost.
t: WordPress Front Page and Posts Page: How to Set Your Homepage and Blog

q: Can I call my blog something other than Blog?
a: Yes. Title the page News, Insights, Advice or anything that suits your business, then assign it as the posts page. The page slug usually sets its address.
t: WordPress Front Page and Posts Page: How to Set Your Homepage and Blog

q: Will changing my homepage setting affect SEO?
a: It can, because it changes what appears at your most important address. A clear, useful homepage can help visitors and search engines understand your business, but plan the change carefully and check that existing links still work.
t: WordPress Front Page and Posts Page: How to Set Your Homepage and Blog

q: Can I change back to latest posts later?
a: Yes. Return to Settings, then Reading, and select Your latest posts. Your pages remain in place, but they will no longer be assigned to those roles.
t: WordPress Front Page and Posts Page: How to Set Your Homepage and Blog

q: Can my homepage be built with a page builder?
a: Generally yes. A page built with a page builder can be assigned as your homepage in the same way as any other published page. Our guide to WordPress page builders covers the wider considerations.
t: WordPress Front Page and Posts Page: How to Set Your Homepage and Blog

q: How long should alt text be?
a: There is no single official limit, but short is generally better. A concise sentence or phrase suits most images. If you need much more, put the detail in the page text.
t: Image Alt Text: How to Write Useful Descriptions for Your Website

q: Does every image need alt text?
a: Every meaningful image needs a useful description. Purely decorative images can usually have empty alt text so that screen readers skip over them.
t: Image Alt Text: How to Write Useful Descriptions for Your Website

q: Does alt text help SEO?
a: It can help search engines understand an image and may support image search visibility. It is one small factor among many, and it should be written for people first.
t: Image Alt Text: How to Write Useful Descriptions for Your Website

q: Should I include keywords in alt text?
a: Only where they naturally describe the image. If your page is about oak dining tables and the photo shows one, saying so is reasonable. Forcing in extra phrases is not.
t: Image Alt Text: How to Write Useful Descriptions for Your Website

q: Can AI write my alt text?
a: It can produce useful first drafts, especially for large catalogues. Review the results, as generated text may not reflect context or may describe details wrongly.
t: Image Alt Text: How to Write Useful Descriptions for Your Website

q: Is alt text a legal requirement in the UK?
a: Requirements depend on your organisation. Public sector websites have specific accessibility rules, and other businesses have wider equality duties. Take legal advice if you are unsure how this applies to you.
t: Image Alt Text: How to Write Useful Descriptions for Your Website

q: Does all my content need to be finished before design starts?
a: Not necessarily. A clear page list, briefs and realistic drafts are often enough to begin. Ask your designer what they need and at what stage, and agree this in your project plan.
t: How to Prepare Your Website Content Before the Build Starts

q: Can a web designer write my content?
a: Some can or will work with a copywriter, while others expect you to supply it. Check this when you get a quote, so it is clear who is responsible and what is included.
t: How to Prepare Your Website Content Before the Build Starts

q: Can I reuse the content from my old website?
a: Yes, if it is still accurate and working well. Review it page by page, because old content may need updating, and be careful about removing pages that bring in search traffic without planning a redirect.
t: How to Prepare Your Website Content Before the Build Starts

q: Can I use stock photos?
a: Yes, if the licence covers your use. They can work well for backgrounds or concepts, but real photos of your people and work are often more convincing where trust matters.
t: How to Prepare Your Website Content Before the Build Starts

q: What format should I send my content in?
a: Editable documents for text and original high-resolution files for images are a sensible default. Your builder may have a preferred template, so ask first.
t: How to Prepare Your Website Content Before the Build Starts

q: What about my privacy policy and terms?
a: These still need attention before launch. Our guide to website terms and privacy policies explains what to consider, and a legal adviser can confirm what your business needs.
t: How to Prepare Your Website Content Before the Build Starts

q: Are accordions bad for SEO?
a: Not inherently. Content in an accordion can still be found if it is present in the page. Keep your most important message visible, and avoid loading text only after a click.
t: Website Accordions and Tabs: When to Use Them and How to Design Them Well

q: Should an FAQ page use an accordion?
a: Often, especially with many questions. With only a few short answers, showing them openly may be easier. See our FAQ page guide for more on this.
t: Website Accordions and Tabs: When to Use Them and How to Design Them Well

q: How many tabs are too many?
a: There is no fixed number. If the labels no longer fit on one row at common screen sizes, or become hard to tell apart, consider an accordion or separate pages.
t: Website Accordions and Tabs: When to Use Them and How to Design Them Well

q: Should the first accordion item be open?
a: It can be helpful, since it shows how the component works and displays useful content immediately. Do so when the first item is relevant to most visitors.
t: Website Accordions and Tabs: When to Use Them and How to Design Them Well

q: Can visitors search for text inside a collapsed panel?
a: It depends on the browser and how the component is built. Some collapsed content may not be found with the browser find function, which is another reason to test important content.
t: Website Accordions and Tabs: When to Use Them and How to Design Them Well

q: Should product details go in tabs or an accordion?
a: Either can work. Accordions often suit mobile shoppers well, but keep key details such as price, size and availability visible rather than hidden in a panel.
t: Website Accordions and Tabs: When to Use Them and How to Design Them Well

q: Does Shopify file my VAT return?
a: No. Shopify calculates tax on orders and provides reports, but you remain responsible for registering, filing and paying. Your accountant or bookkeeper can tell you what records they need.
t: Shopify VAT Settings: How to Set Up Tax on a UK Store

q: Should I add my VAT number if I am not sure I need it?
a: Only enter a number that HMRC has issued to your business. If you are not sure whether you should register, ask an accountant or check HMRC's guidance before you start charging VAT.
t: Shopify VAT Settings: How to Set Up Tax on a UK Store

q: What happens to my prices when I become VAT registered?
a: Your entered prices do not automatically change. You will need to decide whether to raise prices or absorb the VAT from your margin, then update the store settings and pricing at the date your registration takes effect.
t: Shopify VAT Settings: How to Set Up Tax on a UK Store

q: Can I show prices with and without VAT?
a: There are ways to do so, often through theme changes, and this can suit stores with trade and consumer customers. Make sure the page is clear about which price will be charged at checkout.
t: Shopify VAT Settings: How to Set Up Tax on a UK Store

q: Why is the tax in my checkout not what I expected?
a: Check the customer's delivery address, the included-tax setting, whether the product is set to charge tax, any override collections, and the shipping tax setting. Then compare against a simple single-item order.
t: Shopify VAT Settings: How to Set Up Tax on a UK Store

q: Do I need to charge VAT on delivery?
a: Often it follows the treatment of the goods, but mixed orders can complicate this. Ask your accountant to confirm how your store should treat delivery charges.
t: Shopify VAT Settings: How to Set Up Tax on a UK Store

q: Are Shopify analytics accurate?
a: Sales and order figures come directly from your store's records, so they are a strong reference point. Traffic and attribution data are measured by tracking and rely on estimates, so treat them as a guide.
t: Shopify Reports and Analytics: What to Check and What It Means

q: Do I need Google Analytics as well?
a: Many small stores can cover the basics in Shopify. A separate analytics tool can add detail about journeys and content, and it is worth setting up if you will actually use it.
t: Shopify Reports and Analytics: What to Check and What It Means

q: Why can I not see certain reports?
a: Availability depends on your Shopify plan and on your staff permissions. Check your plan's current features and ask the account owner to review your access if needed.
t: Shopify Reports and Analytics: What to Check and What It Means

q: What is a good conversion rate?
a: There is no single right figure, because it varies with products, price, traffic source and device. Your own trend over time, broken down by channel, is usually more useful than a benchmark from elsewhere.
t: Shopify Reports and Analytics: What to Check and What It Means

q: Can I see profit in Shopify?
a: Shopify can show profit-related reports on some plans if you record the cost per item. That still excludes many business expenses, so use your accounts for true profit.
t: Shopify Reports and Analytics: What to Check and What It Means

q: How often should I check my numbers?
a: A weekly look and a deeper monthly review suit many small stores, though busy trading periods may call for closer attention. Choose a routine you will keep up.
t: Shopify Reports and Analytics: What to Check and What It Means

q: Can I undo a Shopify product import?
a: There is no simple undo button. That is why exporting a backup first matters. You can use the backup to restore values by hand or by importing a corrected file.
t: Shopify Product CSV Import and Export: How to Bulk Edit Products Safely

q: Why did my import create duplicate products?
a: Duplicates usually come from changed or mistyped handles. Shopify matches on handle, so a different handle is treated as a new product.
t: Shopify Product CSV Import and Export: How to Bulk Edit Products Safely

q: Why are my images missing after import?
a: The image address may be private, misspelt or no longer available. Shopify needs to reach each image address at the time of import.
t: Shopify Product CSV Import and Export: How to Bulk Edit Products Safely

q: Should I use CSV or the bulk editor?
a: For a handful of changes, the bulk editor is easier to check on screen. For large or repeated changes, or data from another system, a CSV is often quicker.
t: Shopify Product CSV Import and Export: How to Bulk Edit Products Safely

q: Can I update stock levels in the product CSV?
a: Stock is normally managed through the separate inventory export and import, which handles multiple locations more clearly.
t: Shopify Product CSV Import and Export: How to Bulk Edit Products Safely

q: Do I have to transfer my domain to Shopify?
a: No. You can leave the domain with its current registrar and connect it by updating DNS records. Renewal and billing then stay with that registrar.
t: How to Connect a Custom Domain to Shopify Without Breaking Email

q: Will connecting a domain to Shopify stop my email?
a: It should not, provided you only change the web records and leave your MX and related email records alone. Take a copy of your records first and test email afterwards.
t: How to Connect a Custom Domain to Shopify Without Breaking Email

q: Can I use a .co.uk and a .com on the same store?
a: Yes. You can connect both and redirect one to your primary domain, which is a simple way to protect your brand name. Selling to different countries on separate domains is a bigger decision, covered in our guide to selling internationally from a UK online store.
t: How to Connect a Custom Domain to Shopify Without Breaking Email

q: Can I keep my old website on a subdomain?
a: Generally, yes. A subdomain such as blog.yourbrand.co.uk has its own record, so it can point somewhere other than your store. Make sure no records are changed that this subdomain depends on.
t: How to Connect a Custom Domain to Shopify Without Breaking Email

q: Do I need to buy an SSL certificate?
a: Normally not. Shopify provides one automatically for connected domains once the DNS records are correct.
t: How to Connect a Custom Domain to Shopify Without Breaking Email

q: Will changing my domain affect my search rankings?
a: Connecting the address your site already uses is less disruptive than moving to a new one, but replacing an old site still needs redirects and checks. Moving to a new domain is a migration in its own right, and our SEO migration checklist sets out what to protect.
t: How to Connect a Custom Domain to Shopify Without Breaking Email

q: Can I embed my class booking system on my website?
a: Most class booking systems offer a way to embed a timetable or link to a booking page. The design should make that step feel consistent with the rest of the site, and it should work well on mobile.
t: Yoga and Pilates Studio Website Design: Timetables, Classes and Memberships

q: Should a yoga studio website list prices?
a: Generally yes. Clear prices for drop-ins, class packs and memberships help people decide, and terms such as expiry and notice periods should be visible before payment.
t: Yoga and Pilates Studio Website Design: Timetables, Classes and Memberships

q: How can a studio website help beginners?
a: A new students page explaining which classes to start with, what to bring and what to expect, along with clear level labels on the timetable, can help beginners feel confident booking.
t: Yoga and Pilates Studio Website Design: Timetables, Classes and Memberships

q: Can yoga studios make health claims on their website?
a: Describe classes accurately but avoid promising specific health outcomes. Advertising rules apply to website claims, and health claims need to be supportable.
t: Yoga and Pilates Studio Website Design: Timetables, Classes and Memberships

q: Do reformer Pilates studios need different booking features?
a: Reformer classes usually have a fixed number of machines, so booking needs to handle limited capacity, waitlists and late cancellations reliably.
t: Yoga and Pilates Studio Website Design: Timetables, Classes and Memberships

q: Why can I not find the Widgets menu in WordPress?
a: If your site uses a block theme, there is no Widgets menu, because widget areas are replaced by templates and template parts edited in the Site Editor. With a classic theme, the menu sits under Appearance, though some themes have no widget areas at all.
t: WordPress Widgets and Sidebars: How to Use Them Well

q: Can I use blocks in widget areas?
a: Yes. In recent versions of WordPress, the widgets screen in classic themes is block-based, so you can add standard blocks such as paragraphs, images and buttons to widget areas.
t: WordPress Widgets and Sidebars: How to Use Them Well

q: Do sidebars help SEO?
a: A sidebar is not an SEO feature in itself. Sensible internal links in a sidebar can help visitors and search engines discover related content, but a cluttered sidebar full of links adds little. Focus on usefulness to visitors first.
t: WordPress Widgets and Sidebars: How to Use Them Well

q: Will changing my theme delete my widgets?
a: Changing theme does not usually delete widget content outright, but widgets may be moved to an inactive area or placed in different locations because the new theme has different widget areas. Check and rearrange them after any theme change, ideally on a staging copy first.
t: WordPress Widgets and Sidebars: How to Use Them Well

q: Should my homepage have a sidebar?
a: Often not. Homepages tend to work better with a focused, full-width layout that guides visitors towards your main services or products. Sidebars are more commonly useful on blog posts and archive pages.
t: WordPress Widgets and Sidebars: How to Use Them Well

q: How many Administrators should a WordPress site have?
a: As few as practical. Usually the business owner and whoever maintains the site technically. Everyone else should have a lower role suited to their work.
t: WordPress User Roles: How to Give the Right People the Right Access

q: What is the difference between an Editor and an Author?
a: An Editor can publish and edit everyone's posts and pages. An Author can only publish and edit their own posts.
t: WordPress User Roles: How to Give the Right People the Right Access

q: Is it safe to share one login between staff?
a: It is not recommended. Shared logins make it impossible to see who changed what and hard to remove one person's access. Give each person their own account.
t: WordPress User Roles: How to Give the Right People the Right Access

q: What happens to posts when I delete a user?
a: WordPress asks whether to delete their content or attribute it to another user. Choose to attribute it to another account unless you genuinely want the content removed.
t: WordPress User Roles: How to Give the Right People the Right Access

q: Can I create my own user roles?
a: Yes, with a role management plugin or custom code. Keep changes minimal, document them and test with a dummy account first.
t: WordPress User Roles: How to Give the Right People the Right Access

q: Can Prism Works Studio review our WordPress access?
a: Yes. Prism Works Studio can review your user accounts and roles and recommend a safer setup as part of our website and ecommerce development work.
t: WordPress User Roles: How to Give the Right People the Right Access

q: How long do items stay in the WordPress trash?
a: WordPress removes trashed items automatically after a default period, which developers can change. If you need something back, restore it as soon as you notice it is missing.
t: WordPress Trash: How to Restore Deleted Pages, Posts and Media

q: Why did my restored page come back as a draft?
a: Recent versions of WordPress restore trashed content as a draft so you can review it before it goes live again. Check the content and publish it when ready.
t: WordPress Trash: How to Restore Deleted Pages, Posts and Media

q: Can I recover an image I deleted from the media library?
a: Media deletions are usually permanent by default. The main options are restoring from a backup or re-uploading the original file.
t: WordPress Trash: How to Restore Deleted Pages, Posts and Media

q: Does deleting a page affect my search rankings?
a: It can, if the page received visits from search or links from other sites. Restoring it quickly, or redirecting it to a relevant alternative, helps reduce the impact.
t: WordPress Trash: How to Restore Deleted Pages, Posts and Media

q: Who can delete content in WordPress?
a: It depends on user roles. Administrators and editors can usually delete most content, while authors and contributors have more limited permissions over their own work.
t: WordPress Trash: How to Restore Deleted Pages, Posts and Media

q: What is the difference between a synced and an unsynced pattern?
a: A synced pattern stays linked everywhere it is used, so editing it updates every copy. An unsynced pattern inserts independent copies of its blocks, which can each be edited without affecting the original or other copies.
t: WordPress Synced Patterns: How to Reuse Content Without Copying It

q: What happened to reusable blocks in WordPress?
a: Reusable blocks were renamed and became synced patterns. They work in a similar way, and existing reusable blocks on older sites should appear among your patterns.
t: WordPress Synced Patterns: How to Reuse Content Without Copying It

q: Can I change a synced pattern on just one page?
a: You can detach the pattern on that page, which turns it into regular blocks you can edit freely. That copy will no longer receive future updates. Some recent WordPress versions also allow selected parts of a synced pattern to be overridden per page, depending on your setup.
t: WordPress Synced Patterns: How to Reuse Content Without Copying It

q: Do patterns work with classic themes?
a: Patterns are a block editor feature, so they are available wherever you use the block editor for posts and pages, including on sites with classic themes. Managing patterns through the Site Editor applies to block themes.
t: WordPress Synced Patterns: How to Reuse Content Without Copying It

q: Will deleting a synced pattern remove it from my pages?
a: Deleting a synced pattern that is still in use can leave affected pages with missing content or an error message in its place. Check where a pattern is used, and replace or detach those instances, before deleting it.
t: WordPress Synced Patterns: How to Reuse Content Without Copying It

q: Where is Site Health in WordPress?
a: Go to Tools, then Site Health, in the WordPress dashboard. You need an administrator account to see it.
t: WordPress Site Health Screen: How to Read It and What to Do About It

q: Do I need to fix every Site Health recommendation?
a: Not always. Critical issues deserve prompt attention, while recommended improvements can be weighed up and planned into maintenance. Some may not apply to your setup.
t: WordPress Site Health Screen: How to Read It and What to Do About It

q: Is it safe to upgrade PHP when Site Health suggests it?
a: It is usually worthwhile, but check that your theme and extensions support the newer version, take a backup and test on staging first.
t: WordPress Site Health Screen: How to Read It and What to Do About It

q: Does Site Health check for malware?
a: No. It checks configuration and settings, but it does not scan for malware or confirm that a site is clean.
t: WordPress Site Health Screen: How to Read It and What to Do About It

q: Should I share my Site Health info with a developer?
a: It can speed up troubleshooting. Read it first, as it includes server details, and share it only with people you trust.
t: WordPress Site Health Screen: How to Read It and What to Do About It

q: What is the difference between a template and a template part?
a: A template is the full layout for a type of page. A template part is a section, such as a header or footer, that can be reused inside several templates.
t: WordPress Site Editor Templates and Template Parts: A Practical Guide

q: Is a synced pattern the same as a template part?
a: They behave similarly because both update everywhere when edited, but synced patterns are designed for content inside pages, while template parts are part of the site's layout structure.
t: WordPress Site Editor Templates and Template Parts: A Practical Guide

q: Will editing a template change every page?
a: It changes every page that uses that template. Check which template a page uses before editing, and test larger changes on a staging site.
t: WordPress Site Editor Templates and Template Parts: A Practical Guide

q: Can I undo changes to a template?
a: In most cases you can reset a customised template to the theme's original version, but this removes your edits. Keep a backup and a note of changes before making large adjustments.
t: WordPress Site Editor Templates and Template Parts: A Practical Guide

q: Does my site use the site editor?
a: Only if it uses a block theme. Classic themes manage layout differently, usually through theme files, the customiser and widgets.
t: WordPress Site Editor Templates and Template Parts: A Practical Guide

q: Do global styles work with classic themes?
a: No. The Styles panel is part of the Site Editor, which is available with block themes. Classic themes use the Customizer or their own settings instead.
t: WordPress Site Editor Styles: Managing Global Fonts and Colours

q: Will updating my theme remove my style changes?
a: Changes made in the Styles panel are stored separately in the database, so a theme update should not remove them. Theme defaults you have not customised may change, so review the site after updates.
t: WordPress Site Editor Styles: Managing Global Fonts and Colours

q: Can I upload my brand font?
a: Recent WordPress versions let you upload font files through the font library. Check that your font licence allows web use first.
t: WordPress Site Editor Styles: Managing Global Fonts and Colours

q: How do I undo a style change?
a: Use the revision history in the Styles panel to restore an earlier version, or reset to theme defaults if you want to start again.
t: WordPress Site Editor Styles: Managing Global Fonts and Colours

q: Should editors be able to pick any colour?
a: Usually not. Restricting choices to a brand palette keeps the site consistent and helps make sure colour combinations remain readable.
t: WordPress Site Editor Styles: Managing Global Fonts and Colours

q: Does WordPress have built-in search?
a: Yes. WordPress includes a basic search that looks at the titles, content and excerpts of published posts and pages, displayed using your theme's search template.
t: WordPress Search Results Page: Helping Visitors Find What They Need

q: Can I edit the search results page without code?
a: On a block theme, you can edit the search results template in the site editor. On a classic theme, changes usually need a developer working in a child theme.
t: WordPress Search Results Page: Helping Visitors Find What They Need

q: Should search results pages be indexed by Google?
a: Generally not. Internal search pages can create many thin pages, so many sites set them to noindex. Check how your setup handles this.
t: WordPress Search Results Page: Helping Visitors Find What They Need

q: How do I remove certain pages from search results?
a: This normally involves adjusting the search query or using settings in your search setup. Ask your developer to make the change and test it.
t: WordPress Search Results Page: Helping Visitors Find What They Need

q: What should the no results page say?
a: Repeat the search term, suggest alternative searches, show the search box again and link to key pages and your contact details.
t: WordPress Search Results Page: Helping Visitors Find What They Need

q: How can I see what visitors search for?
a: Many analytics setups can record site search terms. Once enabled, review them regularly for patterns and gaps.
t: WordPress Search Results Page: Helping Visitors Find What They Need

q: Why does my scheduled post say "Missed schedule"?
a: WordPress did not run its publishing task at the scheduled time. Common reasons include a timezone mismatch, caching, the task runner being disabled without a replacement, or the server blocking the site's internal request. Publish it manually, then look for the cause.
t: WordPress Scheduled Posts: Scheduling, Timezones and Fixing Missed Schedules

q: Which timezone should a UK WordPress site use?
a: Choose London from the city list in Settings, then General. A fixed UTC offset does not follow the clock changes, so scheduled times will be an hour out for part of the year.
t: WordPress Scheduled Posts: Scheduling, Timezones and Fixing Missed Schedules

q: Can I schedule pages as well as posts?
a: Yes. Pages, and most custom post types that use the standard editor, have the same publish date option.
t: WordPress Scheduled Posts: Scheduling, Timezones and Fixing Missed Schedules

q: Does a scheduled post publish at the exact minute?
a: Not always. With the default setup it publishes on the first visit after the scheduled time. A server task that runs at a fixed interval makes timing more predictable.
t: WordPress Scheduled Posts: Scheduling, Timezones and Fixing Missed Schedules

q: Will scheduling posts improve my SEO?
a: No, scheduling is a workflow tool. It can help you publish consistently, but rankings depend on the quality and usefulness of the content, not on when it was scheduled.
t: WordPress Scheduled Posts: Scheduling, Timezones and Fixing Missed Schedules

q: Can I bulk reschedule posts?
a: The standard quick edit option lets you change dates on posts one at a time from the posts list. For larger changes, plan carefully and test on a staging copy first.
t: WordPress Scheduled Posts: Scheduling, Timezones and Fixing Missed Schedules

q: Where are WordPress revisions stored?
a: Revisions are stored in your site's database as special entries linked to the original post. They are not visible to visitors and do not create separate pages on your site.
t: WordPress Revisions and Autosave: How to Recover and Compare Content

q: Do revisions slow down my website?
a: Revisions are not loaded when visitors view your pages, so they do not usually affect front-end speed directly. A very large number of stored revisions can make the database bigger, which is one reason some sites choose to limit them.
t: WordPress Revisions and Autosave: How to Recover and Compare Content

q: Can I recover a deleted post?
a: Posts moved to the Bin can be restored from there until the Bin is emptied. Once a post is permanently deleted, its revisions go with it, and you would need to restore from a backup.
t: WordPress Revisions and Autosave: How to Recover and Compare Content

q: Why does my page not have any revisions?
a: It may have only been saved once, revisions may be disabled on your site, or the content type may not support them. Your developer or hosting provider can check the configuration.
t: WordPress Revisions and Autosave: How to Recover and Compare Content

q: Does autosave publish my changes?
a: No. On a published post, autosave stores your changes separately and does not alter the live page until you choose to update.
t: WordPress Revisions and Autosave: How to Recover and Compare Content

q: Why is my WordPress site not showing in Google?
a: There can be many reasons, but check the search engine visibility box in Settings, then Reading first. If it is ticked, search engines are being asked not to index the site.
t: WordPress Reading and Discussion Settings: What Each Option Does

q: Why does my blog page ignore the content I added?
a: When a page is set as the posts page, WordPress fills it with your post list and most themes ignore the page's own content. Put introductory text in the theme's archive settings or template instead.
t: WordPress Reading and Discussion Settings: What Each Option Does

q: Should I turn off comments on my business blog?
a: If nobody has time to moderate and reply, turning them off is often better than leaving comments unanswered. You can still invite questions through a contact form.
t: WordPress Reading and Discussion Settings: What Each Option Does

q: Do Discussion settings change existing posts?
a: The default post settings only apply to new posts. Use bulk edit in the posts list to open or close comments on existing posts.
t: WordPress Reading and Discussion Settings: What Each Option Does

q: What are pingbacks and trackbacks?
a: They are notices one site sends to another when it links to it. They are rarely useful for business sites and often attract spam, so many owners switch them off.
t: WordPress Reading and Discussion Settings: What Each Option Does

q: Is the search visibility setting enough to hide a staging site?
a: No. It is a request to search engines, not access control. Use password protection or your host's privacy tools as well.
t: WordPress Reading and Discussion Settings: What Each Option Does

q: How many plugins is too many for WordPress?
a: There is no magic number. What matters is whether each plugin is needed, maintained and well built. A few poorly made plugins can cause more trouble than many good ones.
t: WordPress Plugin Audit: How to Review, Remove and Replace Plugins

q: Is it safe to delete inactive plugins?
a: Usually yes, if you are sure they are not needed. Take a backup first and check whether the plugin stores data you want to keep.
t: WordPress Plugin Audit: How to Review, Remove and Replace Plugins

q: How do I know if a plugin is abandoned?
a: Check its last update date and whether it is marked as tested with recent WordPress versions. Long gaps without updates suggest it may no longer be maintained.
t: WordPress Plugin Audit: How to Review, Remove and Replace Plugins

q: Can removing a plugin break my site?
a: It can, if something depends on it. That is why you should back up, test on staging and remove plugins one at a time.
t: WordPress Plugin Audit: How to Review, Remove and Replace Plugins

q: Do plugins slow WordPress down?
a: Some do, particularly those that load scripts on every page. Removing unnecessary plugins is often one of the simpler ways to lighten a site.
t: WordPress Plugin Audit: How to Review, Remove and Replace Plugins

q: Can Prism Works Studio audit my plugins?
a: Yes. We can review your WordPress site and talk through what to keep, replace or remove. Get in touch via our contact page.
t: WordPress Plugin Audit: How to Review, Remove and Replace Plugins

q: What is the best permalink structure for WordPress?
a: There is no single best option, but the post name structure is a sensible default for many business sites because it is short and readable. News-style sites may prefer a date-based structure.
t: WordPress Permalink Settings: How to Choose and Change Your URL Structure

q: Is it safe to change permalinks in WordPress?
a: On a new site it is low risk. On an established site it changes URLs, so back up first, test on staging and set up redirects from old URLs to new ones.
t: WordPress Permalink Settings: How to Choose and Change Your URL Structure

q: Why are my WordPress pages showing not found after a change?
a: The rewrite rules may need refreshing. Visiting Settings, then Permalinks, and saving without changes often fixes it.
t: WordPress Permalink Settings: How to Choose and Change Your URL Structure

q: Should I include the category in WordPress URLs?
a: It can add context, but if you reorganise categories later the URLs will change. A simpler structure is less fragile if your categories are still evolving.
t: WordPress Permalink Settings: How to Choose and Change Your URL Structure

q: Can I change the slug of a single post?
a: Yes, in the post settings panel of the editor. If the post is already live, add a redirect from the old URL to the new one.
t: WordPress Permalink Settings: How to Choose and Change Your URL Structure

q: Is WordPress Multisite free?
a: Yes, Multisite is a built-in feature of WordPress. You will still need suitable hosting, and some premium plugins license network use differently, so check their terms.
t: WordPress Multisite Explained: Pros, Cons and Alternatives

q: Can each Multisite site have its own domain name?
a: Yes. Current versions of WordPress support mapping custom domains to individual sites in a network, subject to your hosting and DNS setup.
t: WordPress Multisite Explained: Pros, Cons and Alternatives

q: Can each site use different plugins?
a: Plugins are installed once for the network, but the Super Admin can allow individual sites to activate them separately, so sites can use different combinations.
t: WordPress Multisite Explained: Pros, Cons and Alternatives

q: Is Multisite less secure than separate sites?
a: Not inherently, but a vulnerability or fault can affect every site at once. Strong security practice and careful update testing are especially important.
t: WordPress Multisite Explained: Pros, Cons and Alternatives

q: Can I run WooCommerce on Multisite?
a: WooCommerce can run on a Multisite network, with each site acting as a separate store. Check compatibility of any extensions you rely on before committing.
t: WordPress Multisite Explained: Pros, Cons and Alternatives

q: Why can I not find the Menus option in WordPress?
a: If Appearance does not show a Menus option, your site is most likely using a block theme. In that case, menus are managed through the Navigation block in the Site Editor instead.
t: WordPress Menus: A Practical Guide to Building Site Navigation

q: Can I have different menus on different pages?
a: Yes, though how you do it depends on your theme. Block themes let you use different template parts with different Navigation blocks. Classic themes may need theme options or custom development to show different menus on specific pages.
t: WordPress Menus: A Practical Guide to Building Site Navigation

q: How many items should a main menu have?
a: There is no fixed number. Aim for a menu visitors can scan quickly, focused on the main things they come to your site for, and move secondary links elsewhere.
t: WordPress Menus: A Practical Guide to Building Site Navigation

q: Does the menu affect SEO?
a: Menus help search engines discover and understand your important pages, because they are linked from every page. Clear, descriptive labels and a sensible structure help both visitors and search engines.
t: WordPress Menus: A Practical Guide to Building Site Navigation

q: Will changing my menu break anything?
a: Changing menu items does not change page addresses, so it should not break links elsewhere. However, removing a page from the menu can make it harder to find, so make sure important content is still linked from somewhere.
t: WordPress Menus: A Practical Guide to Building Site Navigation

q: Can I create folders in the WordPress media library?
a: Not by default. WordPress organises uploads by date behind the scenes. Folders can be added with a media organisation tool if your library is large.
t: WordPress Media Library Organisation: A Practical Guide

q: Is it safe to delete unused images?
a: It can be, but check carefully first. Images may be used in places WordPress does not track, so back up and test before deleting.
t: WordPress Media Library Organisation: A Practical Guide

q: Does the file name of an image matter for SEO?
a: A descriptive file name, along with good alt text, helps search engines understand an image. It is a small but worthwhile habit.
t: WordPress Media Library Organisation: A Practical Guide

q: What should alt text say?
a: Describe what the image shows and why it is on the page, briefly and naturally. Decorative images can have empty alt text.
t: WordPress Media Library Organisation: A Practical Guide

q: Why are there so many copies of each image?
a: WordPress creates resized versions of each uploaded image for different parts of your theme. This is normal behaviour.
t: WordPress Media Library Organisation: A Practical Guide

q: What size should I upload images to WordPress?
a: It depends on the largest space the image appears in on your theme. Resize to suit that space, allowing for high-density screens, rather than uploading full camera files.
t: WordPress Image Sizes and Thumbnails: How to Get Them Right

q: What is the difference between a featured image and a thumbnail?
a: A featured image is the main image chosen for a post. WordPress calls it a post thumbnail in code, and themes display it in various sizes, including the small thumbnail size.
t: WordPress Image Sizes and Thumbnails: How to Get Them Right

q: Why do my old images look wrong after changing theme?
a: Existing images keep the sizes created when they were uploaded. Regenerating image sizes creates new copies that match the new theme.
t: WordPress Image Sizes and Thumbnails: How to Get Them Right

q: Can I stop WordPress creating so many image sizes?
a: Some sizes can be changed or disabled, but themes may rely on them. Check what your theme uses before removing any sizes, ideally with developer help.
t: WordPress Image Sizes and Thumbnails: How to Get Them Right

q: Does WordPress compress images automatically?
a: WordPress applies some compression to resized copies, but compressing images before upload usually gives you more control over quality and file size.
t: WordPress Image Sizes and Thumbnails: How to Get Them Right

q: Do web fonts slow down a WordPress site?
a: They add files the browser must download, so they can. The effect depends on how many families and weights you use and how they are loaded. A small, well-chosen set has a modest impact.
t: WordPress Font Loading: How to Use Web Fonts Without Slowing Your Site

q: Is it better to host fonts locally?
a: Often, yes. Local hosting avoids an extra connection to another server and keeps visitor data away from third parties. Check the font's licence allows self-hosting.
t: WordPress Font Loading: How to Use Web Fonts Without Slowing Your Site

q: Why does my text change font after the page loads?
a: The browser is showing a fallback font while the web font downloads, then swapping. Choosing a closer fallback and preloading key fonts can reduce how noticeable this is.
t: WordPress Font Loading: How to Use Web Fonts Without Slowing Your Site

q: Can I use any font I like on my website?
a: Only if the licence allows web use. Some fonts are free for web use, others need a paid licence, and desktop licences do not always cover websites.
t: WordPress Font Loading: How to Use Web Fonts Without Slowing Your Site

q: How many fonts should a small business website use?
a: There is no rule, but one or two families with a few weights is enough for most designs and keeps loading light.
t: WordPress Font Loading: How to Use Web Fonts Without Slowing Your Site

q: Will changing fonts affect my search rankings?
a: Fonts themselves are not a ranking factor, but page experience can play a part. Faster, more stable pages are better for visitors either way.
t: WordPress Font Loading: How to Use Web Fonts Without Slowing Your Site

q: Is it safe to clean a WordPress database?
a: It can be, provided you take a full tested backup first and stick to well-understood tasks such as removing spam, trash and expired transients. Deleting tables or options needs more care.
t: WordPress Database Cleanup: How to Tidy Up Safely

q: Should I delete all post revisions?
a: Not necessarily. Revisions let you roll back changes. Many site owners keep a few recent revisions per page and remove older ones.
t: WordPress Database Cleanup: How to Tidy Up Safely

q: Do deleted plugins leave data behind?
a: They can. Some plugins remove their data on uninstall, while others leave tables and options in place unless you remove them separately.
t: WordPress Database Cleanup: How to Tidy Up Safely

q: Will cleaning my database improve SEO?
a: Not directly. It may help performance in some cases, which supports a good visitor experience, but content, structure and technical health matter far more for search.
t: WordPress Database Cleanup: How to Tidy Up Safely

q: Can I clean a WooCommerce store database?
a: Yes, with extra caution. Order and customer data may be needed for accounts and customer service, so check what you need to keep before removing anything.
t: WordPress Database Cleanup: How to Tidy Up Safely

q: Do I need a developer to create custom post types?
a: Not necessarily. Plugins can create them through a settings screen. A developer is useful when you need custom templates, complex fields or a clean, plugin-light setup.
t: WordPress Custom Post Types: When and How to Use Them

q: Will I lose content if I remove a custom post type?
a: Unregistering a post type hides it, but the content generally remains in the database. Registering it again with the same name usually brings it back. Always take a backup before making structural changes.
t: WordPress Custom Post Types: When and How to Use Them

q: Can custom post types use the block editor?
a: Yes, provided the post type is registered with REST API support and the editor feature enabled. Without that, WordPress falls back to the classic editing screen.
t: WordPress Custom Post Types: When and How to Use Them

q: What is the difference between a custom post type and a custom field?
a: A custom post type is a new kind of content, such as Projects. Custom fields are individual pieces of information attached to content, such as a project's location or completion photos.
t: WordPress Custom Post Types: When and How to Use Them

q: Are custom post types good for SEO?
a: They are neutral in themselves. They can help by giving content clear structure, logical URLs and dedicated templates, but the quality of the content still matters most.
t: WordPress Custom Post Types: When and How to Use Them

q: How do I stop spam comments in WordPress?
a: Use the discussion settings to require approval and hold comments with links, add spam filtering if comments are active, or switch comments off if you do not need them.
t: WordPress Comment Spam: How to Reduce It and Manage Comments

q: Should a business website allow comments?
a: It depends. If readers genuinely use comments to ask questions, they can be valuable. If not, switching them off saves time and removes a spam route.
t: WordPress Comment Spam: How to Reduce It and Manage Comments

q: What are trackbacks and pingbacks?
a: They are notifications sent when another site links to your content. They are frequently abused by spammers, and many sites switch them off.
t: WordPress Comment Spam: How to Reduce It and Manage Comments

q: Does comment spam affect SEO?
a: Published spam with low-quality links can make a page look poorly maintained. Keeping spam unpublished avoids that risk.
t: WordPress Comment Spam: How to Reduce It and Manage Comments

q: Should I delete spam comments?
a: Yes, periodically. Check for genuine comments caught by mistake, then empty the spam folder to keep your database tidy.
t: WordPress Comment Spam: How to Reduce It and Manage Comments

q: Will a child theme slow my site down?
a: A properly built child theme adds very little overhead, because it mostly reuses the parent's files. Speed problems usually come from heavy themes, plugins or images rather than the child theme itself.
t: WordPress Child Themes: When You Need One and How to Use It Safely

q: Can I add a child theme to an existing site?
a: Yes. You can create and activate a child theme at any point. Test on staging first, because classic themes may need menus or widgets reassigned after switching.
t: WordPress Child Themes: When You Need One and How to Use It Safely

q: What if my parent theme was edited directly?
a: Identify the changes, ideally by comparing the edited files with a fresh copy of the same theme version, then move them into a child theme or a custom plugin before updating the parent.
t: WordPress Child Themes: When You Need One and How to Use It Safely

q: Do block themes still need child themes?
a: Not always. Many changes can be made in the Site Editor. A child block theme is useful when you want templates and settings stored as files that can be tracked and deployed.
t: WordPress Child Themes: When You Need One and How to Use It Safely

q: Should custom functionality go in the child theme?
a: Only if it is genuinely part of the design. Features you would want to keep after changing theme, such as custom post types, usually belong in a plugin.
t: WordPress Child Themes: When You Need One and How to Use It Safely

q: Can Prism Works Studio set up or clean up a child theme?
a: Yes. Prism Works Studio can audit theme changes, move customisations into a child theme or plugin and test updates as part of our website and ecommerce development work.
t: WordPress Child Themes: When You Need One and How to Use It Safely

q: Should I use categories or tags?
a: Use categories for every post to define its main section. Tags are optional and best used for specific details shared by several posts.
t: WordPress Categories and Tags: Organising Your Blog for Readers and Search

q: How many categories should a blog have?
a: There is no fixed number. Aim for a small set of distinct topics that you will write about regularly.
t: WordPress Categories and Tags: Organising Your Blog for Readers and Search

q: Can a post have more than one category?
a: Yes, but giving each post one main category usually keeps the structure clearer.
t: WordPress Categories and Tags: Organising Your Blog for Readers and Search

q: Are tag pages bad for SEO?
a: Not in themselves, but many thin tag pages with only one or two posts can add little value. Keep tags purposeful and consider your indexing settings.
t: WordPress Categories and Tags: Organising Your Blog for Readers and Search

q: What happens to posts if I delete a category?
a: Posts left with no category are moved to the default category. Reassign posts to the right category before deleting, and redirect the old archive if needed.
t: WordPress Categories and Tags: Organising Your Blog for Readers and Search

q: Is Gutenberg the same as the block editor?
a: Yes, in everyday use. Gutenberg was the name of the project that developed the block editor, and people still use the two names interchangeably.
t: The WordPress Block Editor: A Practical Guide for Site Owners

q: Will switching to the block editor break my existing pages?
a: Existing content is usually kept inside a Classic block and continues to display. You can convert it to blocks when you are ready, checking the result as you go.
t: The WordPress Block Editor: A Practical Guide for Site Owners

q: What is the difference between a pattern and a synced pattern?
a: An unsynced pattern is a starting layout you edit freely after inserting. A synced pattern stays linked, so editing it updates every place it appears.
t: The WordPress Block Editor: A Practical Guide for Site Owners

q: Do I need a block theme to use the block editor?
a: No. Classic themes support the block editor for post and page content. Block themes additionally let you edit headers, footers and templates with blocks.
t: The WordPress Block Editor: A Practical Guide for Site Owners

q: Can I restrict what editors can change?
a: Yes. Developers can limit available blocks, lock blocks and patterns, and set global styles so editors work within a defined design.
t: The WordPress Block Editor: A Practical Guide for Site Owners

q: Are WordPress automatic updates safe?
a: They are generally reliable, and minor core updates are designed to be low risk. Any update can occasionally cause a conflict, so backups and monitoring are important.
t: WordPress Automatic Updates: Core, Plugins and Themes Explained

q: Should I turn on auto-updates for all plugins?
a: Not necessarily. Many sites enable them for simple plugins and update critical ones, such as ecommerce or forms, manually after testing.
t: WordPress Automatic Updates: Core, Plugins and Themes Explained

q: Why can I not see the auto-update option?
a: Your host or developer may control updates at the server or configuration level, which can hide or override the dashboard settings.
t: WordPress Automatic Updates: Core, Plugins and Themes Explained

q: What happens if an automatic update breaks my site?
a: WordPress may send a recovery mode email to the admin address so you can deactivate the problem. You can also restore from a backup.
t: WordPress Automatic Updates: Core, Plugins and Themes Explained

q: Do I still need to check my site if updates are automatic?
a: Yes. Automatic updates save time, but a regular check of key pages and forms makes sure nothing has quietly stopped working.
t: WordPress Automatic Updates: Core, Plugins and Themes Explained

q: Does every website need a privacy policy?
a: If your site collects personal data, which includes contact forms and many analytics tools, you will generally need to provide privacy information. Check the ICO's guidance for your circumstances.
t: Website Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy: A UK Business Guide

q: Can I copy another website's terms and conditions?
a: It is not advisable. Their terms reflect their business, not yours, and copying text may also raise copyright issues. Use templates only as a starting point and adapt them properly.
t: Website Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy: A UK Business Guide

q: Do I need terms and conditions for a brochure website?
a: Website terms of use are often optional for a simple brochure site, but a privacy notice is still likely to be needed if you collect personal data.
t: Website Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy: A UK Business Guide

q: Are platform policy templates good enough?
a: They can be a reasonable starting point, but they are generic. Review and adapt them so they accurately describe your business, and take advice if you are unsure.
t: Website Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy: A UK Business Guide

q: Who regulates this in the UK?
a: The ICO covers data protection and cookies. Consumer law is enforced by bodies including the Competition and Markets Authority and Trading Standards.
t: Website Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy: A UK Business Guide

q: What is the easiest way to make a table work on mobile?
a: Wrapping the table in its own horizontally scrolling container is usually simplest. It keeps the table intact while stopping the whole page from scrolling sideways.
t: Website Tables on Mobile: How to Make Tables Readable on Small Screens

q: Should I use an image of a table instead?
a: No. Images of tables cannot be read by screen readers, are hard to update and are often unreadable on phones. Use a real table.
t: Website Tables on Mobile: How to Make Tables Readable on Small Screens

q: How many columns are too many for mobile?
a: It depends on the content. If the table needs a lot of sideways scrolling, consider swapping rows and columns, splitting it or using stacked cards.
t: Website Tables on Mobile: How to Make Tables Readable on Small Screens

q: Do tables affect SEO?
a: Search engines can read properly built tables. A clear, usable table helps visitors, which is the main goal, and a heading above it gives useful context.
t: Website Tables on Mobile: How to Make Tables Readable on Small Screens

q: Can I hide columns on mobile?
a: You can, but only hide genuinely secondary information and provide a clear way to view it. Hiding essential details can frustrate visitors.
t: Website Tables on Mobile: How to Make Tables Readable on Small Screens

q: Is a pricing table the same as a data table?
a: Not always. Package comparisons are often better as cards with feature lists. Our pricing page design guide covers that layout.
t: Website Tables on Mobile: How to Make Tables Readable on Small Screens

q: Are sticky headers good for SEO?
a: A sticky header does not directly affect rankings. It can support a better visitor experience, but a header that causes layout shifts or hides content could work against you, so focus on usability.
t: Sticky Header Design: Keeping Navigation Close Without Getting in the Way

q: Should my sticky header include a call to action?
a: If your site has one clear primary action, such as booking or enquiring, a compact button in the sticky header can be useful. Avoid adding several competing buttons.
t: Sticky Header Design: Keeping Navigation Close Without Getting in the Way

q: What is better: always visible or reveal on scroll up?
a: It depends on the site. Reveal on scroll up gives more room for content and suits reading pages and mobile. Always visible suits stores where search and basket are used often. Testing with real visitors is the best guide.
t: Sticky Header Design: Keeping Navigation Close Without Getting in the Way

q: Why do my anchor links hide headings under the header?
a: Fixed headers overlap the top of the screen, so the browser scrolls the heading under them. Adding a scroll offset in your site styles usually solves this.
t: Sticky Header Design: Keeping Navigation Close Without Getting in the Way

q: Do sticky headers work with mega menus?
a: They can, but large dropdowns need to fit within the screen and scroll if necessary. Test them carefully on smaller laptop screens. Our guide to website navigation structure covers menu planning.
t: Sticky Header Design: Keeping Navigation Close Without Getting in the Way

q: Can I turn off the sticky header on some pages?
a: Often yes, depending on your theme. Landing pages and checkout flows sometimes benefit from a simpler header, so it is worth checking what your theme allows.
