q: Can I import redirects in bulk?
a: Yes. Shopify lets you import a CSV file with the old paths and new destinations from the URL redirects screen.
t: Shopify URL Redirects: When to Use Them and How to Set Them Up

q: Does Shopify create redirects automatically?
a: When you change a handle, Shopify offers to create a redirect from the old address, usually ticked by default. It does not create redirects when you delete items.
t: Shopify URL Redirects: When to Use Them and How to Set Them Up

q: Do redirects hurt SEO?
a: Well-planned redirects protect search visibility when addresses change. Problems come from chains, loops and redirecting unrelated pages to the homepage.
t: Shopify URL Redirects: When to Use Them and How to Set Them Up

q: Do Shopify themes update automatically?
a: No. Shopify notifies you when an update is available, and you choose when to add the updated version and publish it.
t: Shopify Theme Updates: How to Update Your Theme Safely

q: Will I lose my customisations when I update?
a: Settings and content made through the theme editor usually carry over. Direct code edits generally need to be reapplied to the new version.
t: Shopify Theme Updates: How to Update Your Theme Safely

q: How do I know what changed in an update?
a: Check the release notes published by the theme developer, usually linked from the theme listing or the update notification.
t: Shopify Theme Updates: How to Update Your Theme Safely

q: Can I go back if the update causes problems?
a: Yes, if you keep your previous theme in the library. You can republish it while you fix issues in the updated copy.
t: Shopify Theme Updates: How to Update Your Theme Safely

q: Do I need a developer to update my theme?
a: Not always. A theme with only settings-based changes can often be updated by the store owner. Themes with code edits usually benefit from developer help.
t: Shopify Theme Updates: How to Update Your Theme Safely

q: What is the difference between a section and a block in Shopify?
a: A section is a full width band on a page, such as a slideshow or featured collection. A block is a smaller piece of content within a section, such as a single slide, heading or button.
t: Shopify Theme Sections and Blocks: How to Build Flexible Pages

q: Can I add sections to product pages?
a: In most modern themes, yes. You can add sections below the main product area and reorder the blocks within the product information section.
t: Shopify Theme Sections and Blocks: How to Build Flexible Pages

q: Do I need a developer to use sections?
a: No. Adding, reordering and configuring sections and blocks is done in the theme editor without code. A developer is only needed for custom sections or features your theme does not provide.
t: Shopify Theme Sections and Blocks: How to Build Flexible Pages

q: Will my sections be lost if I change theme?
a: Section content is usually tied to the theme, so switching to a different theme generally means rebuilding layouts. Product data, collections and metafields remain in your store.
t: Shopify Theme Sections and Blocks: How to Build Flexible Pages

q: How many sections should a page have?
a: There is no fixed number. Include the sections shoppers need to make a decision, and remove those that add length without helping.
t: Shopify Theme Sections and Blocks: How to Build Flexible Pages

q: Can sections show different content on each product?
a: Yes, by connecting settings to dynamic sources such as metafields, one template can display product-specific content.
t: Shopify Theme Sections and Blocks: How to Build Flexible Pages

q: Can I just use the Shopify policy templates?
a: They are a useful starting point, but they are generic. Edit them to reflect how your business works and consider getting them reviewed by a qualified professional.
t: Shopify Store Policies: Setting Up Refund, Privacy and Shipping Pages

q: Where should policies appear on my store?
a: Link them in the footer, check they appear at checkout and add short delivery and returns summaries to product pages.
t: Shopify Store Policies: Setting Up Refund, Privacy and Shipping Pages

q: Do I need a privacy policy for a small shop?
a: If you collect personal data, which any store taking orders does, data protection rules may require you to explain how you use it. Take advice on what applies to your business.
t: Shopify Store Policies: Setting Up Refund, Privacy and Shipping Pages

q: Can my returns policy override customer rights?
a: Generally no. Statutory consumer rights may still apply regardless of what your policy says. Your policy can offer more, but should not suggest customers have fewer rights.
t: Shopify Store Policies: Setting Up Refund, Privacy and Shipping Pages

q: How often should I review my policies?
a: Whenever your shipping, returns, apps or markets change, and on a regular schedule in between.
t: Shopify Store Policies: Setting Up Refund, Privacy and Shipping Pages

q: How many staff accounts can I have on Shopify?
a: It depends on your plan, and Shopify updates its plans periodically. Check your current plan in the Shopify admin or on Shopify's pricing information.
t: Shopify Staff Accounts: Managing Access to Your Store Safely

q: What is the difference between a staff account and a collaborator account?
a: Staff accounts are for your own team. Collaborator accounts are for agencies and developers working through Shopify's partner system, and you approve and remove them yourself.
t: Shopify Staff Accounts: Managing Access to Your Store Safely

q: Can I limit what a staff member can see?
a: Yes. When inviting or editing a staff member, choose only the permissions they need, such as orders and products, and leave everything else switched off.
t: Shopify Staff Accounts: Managing Access to Your Store Safely

q: What should I do when a staff member leaves?
a: Remove or suspend their Shopify account promptly and review any connected apps or services they could access.
t: Shopify Staff Accounts: Managing Access to Your Store Safely

q: Can I transfer store ownership?
a: Yes. The current store owner can transfer ownership to another staff member through the store's user settings, subject to Shopify's requirements.
t: Shopify Staff Accounts: Managing Access to Your Store Safely

q: Can a product belong to more than one shipping profile?
a: No. Each product sits in one profile at a time. Moving it into a custom profile removes it from the general profile's rates.
t: Shopify Shipping Profiles: How to Set Different Rates for Different Products

q: Do I need shipping profiles for a small store?
a: Not necessarily. If your products are similar in size and ship the same way, the general profile alone may be all you need. Add custom profiles only when there is a clear reason.
t: Shopify Shipping Profiles: How to Set Different Rates for Different Products

q: Why is shipping higher when customers buy items from different profiles?
a: Shopify combines the rates from each profile in a mixed basket. Test these baskets and adjust your profiles or rates if the totals do not reflect your real costs.
t: Shopify Shipping Profiles: How to Set Different Rates for Different Products

q: Can I offer free shipping on only some products?
a: Yes. Placing those products in their own profile with a free rate is one way to do it. Check how mixed baskets behave afterwards.
t: Shopify Shipping Profiles: How to Set Different Rates for Different Products

q: How often should I review shipping profiles?
a: Review them whenever you change carriers, add a product range or start selling to new regions, and periodically in case carrier prices have changed.
t: Shopify Shipping Profiles: How to Set Different Rates for Different Products

q: Does Shopify include search by default?
a: Yes. Shopify stores include built-in search, and many themes add predictive search. Shopify's own Search and Discovery app adds further controls such as synonyms, filters and boosts.
t: Shopify Search and Discovery: Setting Up Search That Helps Shoppers

q: What are search synonyms in Shopify?
a: Synonyms are groups of words that search treats as equivalent, so a shopper searching for one term also sees products described with another.
t: Shopify Search and Discovery: Setting Up Search That Helps Shoppers

q: Why are my filters not showing?
a: Filters depend on both your settings and your theme's support for them. Check that filters are enabled, that your theme supports them, and that products have the relevant data filled in.
t: Shopify Search and Discovery: Setting Up Search That Helps Shoppers

q: Can I control which products appear first in search?
a: Product boosts let you promote chosen products for particular search terms. Use them carefully so results stay relevant.
t: Shopify Search and Discovery: Setting Up Search That Helps Shoppers

q: How often should I review search settings?
a: A regular review, plus checks whenever you add new ranges, keeps search working well. The right frequency depends on how often your catalogue changes.
t: Shopify Search and Discovery: Setting Up Search That Helps Shoppers

q: Do I need the online store channel to use Shopify?
a: Not always. Some businesses sell mainly in person or through other channels. However, for most online sellers the online store is the core channel and the one they control most fully.
t: Shopify Sales Channels: How to Sell in More Places From One Store

q: Does stock update across all channels automatically?
a: Inventory is held centrally in Shopify, so sales on connected channels reduce the shared stock count. It is still sensible to check how each specific channel syncs and how quickly updates appear there.
t: Shopify Sales Channels: How to Sell in More Places From One Store

q: Can I show different products on different channels?
a: Yes. Each product's availability can be set per channel, so you can choose exactly which items appear where.
t: Shopify Sales Channels: How to Sell in More Places From One Store

q: Are there extra costs for selling on other channels?
a: Some channels or platforms may charge their own fees or commissions. Check the current terms for each one before you start selling there.
t: Shopify Sales Channels: How to Sell in More Places From One Store

q: Will orders from all channels appear in one place?
a: Orders from connected channels generally appear in your main Shopify orders list, usually labelled with their source, so you can fulfil them from one queue.
t: Shopify Sales Channels: How to Sell in More Places From One Store

q: Can each Shopify variant have its own price?
a: Yes. Each variant can have its own price and compare-at price. Make sure your theme updates the displayed price when the customer changes their selection.
t: Shopify Product Variants: Setting Up Sizes, Colours and Options

q: Does each variant get its own URL?
a: Variants share the main product page. A variant parameter may be added to the URL when an option is selected, but the canonical URL usually stays the main product page.
t: Shopify Product Variants: Setting Up Sizes, Colours and Options

q: Should colours be variants or separate products?
a: It depends on your range. Colours are often variants when everything else is identical. Separate products can make sense when each colour has its own story, photography or search demand.
t: Shopify Product Variants: Setting Up Sizes, Colours and Options

q: How do I stop customers choosing sold-out sizes?
a: Your theme can mark sold-out combinations as unavailable, and some themes can hide them. Check your theme settings, or ask a developer to adjust the product form.
t: Shopify Product Variants: Setting Up Sizes, Colours and Options

q: Can I add personalisation without creating variants?
a: Yes. Line item properties let customers add details such as engraving text to an order without creating extra variants. These usually need a small theme change.
t: Shopify Product Variants: Setting Up Sizes, Colours and Options

q: Can customers see Shopify product tags?
a: Not by default. Some themes display tags or use them for features such as badges, so check your theme to see how tags are used.
t: Shopify Product Tags: A Practical Guide to Naming, Using and Tidying Them

q: Are Shopify tags case sensitive?
a: Small differences in how tags are written can lead to separate-looking tags, which makes the list harder to manage. Agreeing a single convention, such as all lowercase, avoids the problem.
t: Shopify Product Tags: A Practical Guide to Naming, Using and Tidying Them

q: Should I use tags or metafields in Shopify?
a: Tags suit simple labels and collection rules. Metafields are usually better for structured product details that need to be displayed or used in filters.
t: Shopify Product Tags: A Practical Guide to Naming, Using and Tidying Them

q: How do I remove a tag from many products?
a: Select the products in the admin and use the bulk action to remove tags, or use the bulk editor. Check which automated collections use the tag first.
t: Shopify Product Tags: A Practical Guide to Naming, Using and Tidying Them

q: Do product tags help Shopify SEO?
a: Tags rarely have much direct effect. Their main value is organising products into clear collections, which can then be well described and linked.
t: Shopify Product Tags: A Practical Guide to Naming, Using and Tidying Them

q: How many images should a Shopify product have?
a: There is no fixed number. Use enough images to answer the questions a buyer would ask, without repeating near-identical shots. Simple products may need few; complex or variable products may need more.
t: Shopify Product Media: A Guide to Images, Video and 3D Models

q: Can I show different images for each colour?
a: Yes. Assign an image to each variant in Shopify admin. Depending on your theme, selecting a variant will switch the main image or filter the gallery.
t: Shopify Product Media: A Guide to Images, Video and 3D Models

q: Should I use video on every product?
a: Not necessarily. Video is most useful where movement, function or scale is hard to show in photos. For simple products, good photography may be enough.
t: Shopify Product Media: A Guide to Images, Video and 3D Models

q: Do I need alt text on every product image?
a: It is good practice to add meaningful alt text to product images, because they usually carry information. Describe what each specific image shows rather than repeating the product title.
t: Shopify Product Media: A Guide to Images, Video and 3D Models

q: Will 3D models work on every device?
a: No. Viewing in augmented reality depends on the customer's device and browser. Keep standard photographs alongside any 3D model.
t: Shopify Product Media: A Guide to Images, Video and 3D Models

q: Can I reuse the same image on several products?
a: Yes, you can select existing files from your store's file library. This is useful for shared lifestyle images, but each product should still have its own clear main image.
t: Shopify Product Media: A Guide to Images, Video and 3D Models

q: Does Shopify have built-in product filters?
a: Yes. Shopify supports storefront filtering on collection and search pages, configured through the free Search and Discovery app, provided your theme supports it.
t: Shopify Product Filters: Helping Shoppers Narrow Down Choices

q: Why are my Shopify filters not showing?
a: The most likely reasons are that your theme does not support storefront filtering, the filters have not been added in the Search and Discovery app, or products lack the relevant data.
t: Shopify Product Filters: Helping Shoppers Narrow Down Choices

q: Can I filter by custom attributes like material?
a: Yes. Store the attribute in a product or variant metafield of a supported type, then add that metafield as a filter in the Search and Discovery app.
t: Shopify Product Filters: Helping Shoppers Narrow Down Choices

q: Do filtered pages cause duplicate content?
a: They can create many URL variations. Shopify themes usually point canonical tags at the main collection, but it is worth checking your theme's behaviour.
t: Shopify Product Filters: Helping Shoppers Narrow Down Choices

q: Should I use a filter app instead?
a: Only if native filtering cannot meet your needs. Apps can add advanced features, but they also add cost, complexity and another dependency.
t: Shopify Product Filters: Helping Shoppers Narrow Down Choices

q: Can Shopify do pre-orders without an app?
a: For simple pre-orders with full payment upfront, you can use the built-in option to continue selling a variant when it is out of stock, combined with clear product page wording. For deposits, delayed payments or automatic labelling, an app built on Shopify's purchase options is usually needed.
t: Shopify Pre-Orders: A Practical Guide to Selling Before Stock Arrives

q: Should I take full payment for a pre-order?
a: It depends on your product, cash flow and confidence in the arrival date. Full payment is simplest to explain and manage. Deposits or delayed charges can feel lower risk to customers but add extra steps and the chance of a failed payment later.
t: Shopify Pre-Orders: A Practical Guide to Selling Before Stock Arrives

q: How do I stop overselling a pre-order?
a: Set a limit based on the quantity you expect to receive, either through stock levels or the tool you use for pre-orders. Review it as your supplier confirms quantities, and switch the product back to a normal listing once stock arrives.
t: Shopify Pre-Orders: A Practical Guide to Selling Before Stock Arrives

q: What happens if the stock is delayed?
a: Tell affected customers as soon as you know, give a revised estimate and offer them the option to cancel for a refund. Update the product page so that new customers see the new timing too.
t: Shopify Pre-Orders: A Practical Guide to Selling Before Stock Arrives

q: Do pre-orders affect my store's SEO?
a: A pre-order product page can be indexed like any other product page, which can help people find a new product before launch. Keep the page content accurate and avoid deleting it once the product is in stock, so that any visibility it has built carries forward. Our Shopify SEO guide covers product page basics.
t: Shopify Pre-Orders: A Practical Guide to Selling Before Stock Arrives

q: What does fulfilled mean in Shopify?
a: An order is marked as fulfilled when all its physical items have been recorded as sent. It is separate from payment status, so an order can be paid and unfulfilled, or fulfilled and later refunded.
t: Shopify Order Fulfilment Workflow: From New Order to Delivered Parcel

q: Should I use automatic fulfilment in Shopify?
a: Automatic fulfilment can suit digital products. For physical goods, manual fulfilment is usually safer because orders are only marked as sent once someone has packed them.
t: Shopify Order Fulfilment Workflow: From New Order to Delivered Parcel

q: Can I send part of a Shopify order?
a: Yes. You can fulfil some items and leave the rest unfulfilled, and the order will show as partially fulfilled. Tell the customer clearly so they know more is coming.
t: Shopify Order Fulfilment Workflow: From New Order to Delivered Parcel

q: How do I stop an order being packed by mistake?
a: Use the hold option where your setup supports it, or add a consistent tag and exclude tagged orders from the saved view your packers work from.
t: Shopify Order Fulfilment Workflow: From New Order to Delivered Parcel

q: Do I need to add tracking numbers in Shopify?
a: Adding tracking is strongly recommended. It lets customers follow their parcel from the shipping confirmation email and tends to reduce delivery questions.
t: Shopify Order Fulfilment Workflow: From New Order to Delivered Parcel

q: Can I edit an order that has already shipped?
a: Generally, editing applies to unfulfilled items. Once an item has shipped, you would usually handle changes through a return and refund rather than an edit. Check Shopify's current documentation for the exact rules.
t: Shopify Order Editing and Refunds: How to Change Orders Cleanly

q: Does editing an order charge the customer automatically?
a: If an edit increases the total, the customer typically needs to pay the balance, for example through an invoice sent from the order. If it reduces the total, you can refund the difference.
t: Shopify Order Editing and Refunds: How to Change Orders Cleanly

q: Should I restock refunded items straight away?
a: Only restock items that are physically back and sellable. Restocking too early can lead to overselling stock you do not have.
t: Shopify Order Editing and Refunds: How to Change Orders Cleanly

q: Can I refund to a different payment method?
a: Refunds normally go back to the original payment method. If you need to compensate a customer another way, such as with a gift card or store credit, make sure this is consistent with your policy and the customer's rights.
t: Shopify Order Editing and Refunds: How to Change Orders Cleanly

q: Will the customer be notified of a refund?
a: Shopify can send a refund notification, and you can choose whether to send it. It is good practice to notify the customer so they know to expect the money.
t: Shopify Order Editing and Refunds: How to Change Orders Cleanly

q: How do I stop staff issuing refunds without approval?
a: Use staff account permissions to control who can issue refunds and edit orders, and agree a written process for when approval is needed. Our guide to Shopify staff accounts and permissions covers this in more detail.
t: Shopify Order Editing and Refunds: How to Change Orders Cleanly

q: Where do I edit menus in Shopify?
a: In the admin, go to Content, then Menus. On older admin layouts this was under Online Store, then Navigation.
t: Shopify Navigation Menus: How to Set Up and Structure Them

q: Why is my new menu not showing on the store?
a: Menus only appear where the theme displays them. Open the theme editor, select the header or footer section and choose your menu in its settings.
t: Shopify Navigation Menus: How to Set Up and Structure Them

q: How do I create a dropdown menu in Shopify?
a: Add the items to the menu, then drag the child items underneath and slightly to the right of the parent item so they are nested.
t: Shopify Navigation Menus: How to Set Up and Structure Them

q: How many items should my main menu have?
a: There is no fixed number. Keep the top level short enough to fit comfortably on one line on desktop and to scan easily on mobile, and group the rest into dropdowns.
t: Shopify Navigation Menus: How to Set Up and Structure Them

q: Do menu links help SEO?
a: They act as internal links, so linking your key collections from the menu helps search engines understand which pages matter. Keep menus focused rather than linking everything.
t: Shopify Navigation Menus: How to Set Up and Structure Them

q: What happens to menu links when I delete a collection?
a: The menu item may break or disappear depending on the link type. Update the menu and set up a redirect from the old address.
t: Shopify Navigation Menus: How to Set Up and Structure Them

q: Do I need an app to use Shopify metafields?
a: No. You can create metafield definitions and metaobjects in Settings, Custom data, and show them through dynamic sources in compatible themes. Apps are only needed for specialised workflows.
t: Shopify Metafields: How to Add Custom Product Information Without Apps

q: What is the difference between a metafield and a metaobject?
a: A metafield adds one piece of information to a resource, such as a product. A metaobject is a reusable entry with several fields that many resources can reference.
t: Shopify Metafields: How to Add Custom Product Information Without Apps

q: Can customers filter by metafields?
a: Often, yes. Shopify's Search and Discovery app supports certain metafield types as filters. Check which types are supported in the current documentation.
t: Shopify Metafields: How to Add Custom Product Information Without Apps

q: Will metafields work with my theme?
a: Most current Online Store themes support dynamic sources for common blocks. Older or heavily customised themes may need some Liquid code to display metafields.
t: Shopify Metafields: How to Add Custom Product Information Without Apps

q: Should I use tags or metafields?
a: Tags are quick but free-form, so typos slip in. Metafields with defined types and allowed values are usually more reliable for filters and structured product details.
t: Shopify Metafields: How to Add Custom Product Information Without Apps

q: Can Prism Works Studio set up metafields for our store?
a: Yes. Prism Works Studio can plan your custom data, set up metafields and metaobjects and connect them to your theme as part of our website and ecommerce development work.
t: Shopify Metafields: How to Add Custom Product Information Without Apps

q: Is local pickup built into Shopify?
a: Yes. Shopify includes local pickup as a delivery option that you can enable for your locations in the shipping and delivery settings, without needing a separate app for the basic setup.
t: Shopify Local Pickup: How to Offer Click and Collect From Your Shop

q: Can I offer pickup from more than one location?
a: Yes, if you have several locations set up in Shopify you can choose which ones offer pickup. Make sure stock is assigned to each one accurately so that customers only see pickup where items are actually available.
t: Shopify Local Pickup: How to Offer Click and Collect From Your Shop

q: Should I charge for click and collect?
a: That is a business decision. Many stores offer collection at no charge, as it saves on packaging and courier costs, but you can set a fee if that suits you. Whatever you decide, show it clearly at checkout.
t: Shopify Local Pickup: How to Offer Click and Collect From Your Shop

q: Can customers collect from home if I run a home-based business?
a: Technically you can set your home as a location, but think carefully about privacy, safety and practicalities before doing so. Some home-based businesses prefer to offer local delivery or arrange collections only by appointment.
t: Shopify Local Pickup: How to Offer Click and Collect From Your Shop

q: How is local pickup different from local delivery?
a: With local pickup, the customer comes to you to collect the order. With local delivery, you take the order to the customer's address within an area you define. Shopify supports both, and some stores offer each alongside standard shipping.
t: Shopify Local Pickup: How to Offer Click and Collect From Your Shop

q: Do I need inventory transfers if I only have one shop?
a: No. Transfers are for moving stock between two or more Shopify locations. With a single location, you simply adjust inventory when stock arrives or is written off.
t: Shopify Inventory Transfers: Moving Stock Between Locations

q: Can I edit a transfer after creating it?
a: Usually you can edit a transfer before it is marked as sent or received. Once stock has been received, it is generally better to record a correction than to rewrite history. Check Shopify's current documentation for your plan.
t: Shopify Inventory Transfers: Moving Stock Between Locations

q: Why does my product show out of stock online when I have stock?
a: The stock may be at a location that does not fulfil online orders, or it may be in transit on an open transfer. Check each location's settings and any open transfers.
t: Shopify Inventory Transfers: Moving Stock Between Locations

q: Can I transfer stock to a pop-up or market stall?
a: Yes, if you set the pop-up up as a location. Transfer stock out before the event and transfer any unsold items back afterwards, so each location stays accurate.
t: Shopify Inventory Transfers: Moving Stock Between Locations

q: What should I do if items arrive damaged?
a: Do not accept damaged items as sellable stock. Record them as rejected or note the damage when receiving, then decide separately whether to write them off or return them.
t: Shopify Inventory Transfers: Moving Stock Between Locations

q: How often should I count stock at each location?
a: There is no single right answer. Many businesses count fast-moving lines more often than slow ones. Choose a rhythm you can keep up and compare results against Shopify each time.
t: Shopify Inventory Transfers: Moving Stock Between Locations

q: How do I stop Shopify selling out-of-stock products?
a: Turn on quantity tracking for the product and make sure the option to continue selling when out of stock is switched off.
t: Shopify Inventory and Stock Management: The Basics

q: What is a SKU and do I need one?
a: A SKU is your own unique code for each product variant. It is not strictly required, but it makes stock management, counting and reporting far easier.
t: Shopify Inventory and Stock Management: The Basics

q: Can Shopify track stock in more than one location?
a: Yes. Shopify supports multiple locations, each with its own stock levels. The number allowed depends on your plan.
t: Shopify Inventory and Stock Management: The Basics

q: How often should I count stock?
a: It depends on your range and volume. Many shops combine an occasional full count with regular cycle counts of smaller sections.
t: Shopify Inventory and Stock Management: The Basics

q: Why are my Shopify stock levels wrong?
a: Common causes include returns not being restocked correctly, unrecorded breakages or samples, channels not syncing, and import errors.
t: Shopify Inventory and Stock Management: The Basics

q: Can Prism Works Studio help with Shopify inventory setup?
a: Yes. We can review your store's product and inventory setup and talk through options. See our pricing page or get in touch.
t: Shopify Inventory and Stock Management: The Basics

q: Does Shopify have built-in gift wrapping?
a: Shopify does not have a dedicated gift wrapping feature. Most stores offer it as a product, a variant option or through custom cart fields set up in the theme.
t: Shopify Gift Wrapping and Order Notes: How to Offer Gift Options

q: Where do customers' order notes appear?
a: Cart notes and cart attributes appear in the order details in the Shopify admin. They can also be added to packing slips and notification emails by editing the relevant templates.
t: Shopify Gift Wrapping and Order Notes: How to Offer Gift Options

q: Can I hide prices on a gift order?
a: You can edit your packing slip template to leave out prices, either for all orders or for orders marked as gifts. Test it carefully before relying on it.
t: Shopify Gift Wrapping and Order Notes: How to Offer Gift Options

q: Can customers add a different message to each item?
a: Yes, using line item properties, which let customers enter details for individual products. These usually require theme changes to set up.
t: Shopify Gift Wrapping and Order Notes: How to Offer Gift Options

q: Should I charge for gift wrapping?
a: That is a business decision. Some stores include it free as a service, while others charge to cover materials and time. Whatever you choose, make the price clear before checkout.
t: Shopify Gift Wrapping and Order Notes: How to Offer Gift Options

q: Can customers see draft orders?
a: Customers do not see a draft order until you send them an invoice. Once sent, they can view the items and totals through the invoice link and complete payment.
t: Shopify Draft Orders: A Practical Guide for Store Owners

q: Can I edit a draft order after sending the invoice?
a: You can usually edit an open draft order and resend the invoice. Make sure the customer uses the latest invoice link so they see the correct details.
t: Shopify Draft Orders: A Practical Guide for Store Owners

q: Do draft orders count in my sales reports?
a: Draft orders are not counted as sales until they are completed. Once paid or marked as paid, they become normal orders and appear in your reports.
t: Shopify Draft Orders: A Practical Guide for Store Owners

q: Can I add products that are not in my store?
a: Yes. Custom line items let you add items with your own description and price, which is useful for bespoke work or one-off charges.
t: Shopify Draft Orders: A Practical Guide for Store Owners

q: Should every phone order go through draft orders?
a: Draft orders are one option. Depending on your setup, Shopify POS or other tools may suit some in-person or phone sales better. Choose the approach that keeps your records accurate and simple for your team.
t: Shopify Draft Orders: A Practical Guide for Store Owners

q: Do Shopify customer segments update automatically?
a: Yes. Segments are based on conditions, so customers move in and out as their data changes.
t: Shopify Customer Segments: Grouping Customers for Better Marketing

q: How many segments should a store have?
a: There is no set number. Start with a few segments that each support a clear action, and add more only when you have a specific use for them.
t: Shopify Customer Segments: Grouping Customers for Better Marketing

q: Can I give a discount to one segment only?
a: Shopify allows some discounts to be limited to specific customer segments. Check the current discount settings in your admin for the options available.
t: Shopify Customer Segments: Grouping Customers for Better Marketing

q: Can I email everyone in a segment?
a: Only customers who have agreed to receive marketing should get marketing emails. Check subscription status and current UK guidance on direct marketing.
